name: Hime cut

card.summary: A Japanese hairstyle of straight, cheek-length sidelocks and blunt bangs over long straight hair, used to frame the face with a sharp, symmetrical shape.
card.note: Needs straight hair or regular straightening and frequent touch-ups to keep its shape.

quick.overview:
The hime cut pairs blunt bangs and straight sidelocks cut at about cheek level with long, straight hair at the back. The name means princess cut in Japanese, and the look is tied historically to noblewomen of Japan's Heian period.

For appearance, the sidelocks and fringe create a framed, symmetrical outline around the face, so it changes a look with a haircut rather than a procedure.
quick.how: A stylist cuts the front fringe straight across and the side sections straight at cheek or jaw length, leaving the back long. People with wavy or curly hair typically maintain the shape with straightening tools or treatments, and the fringe needs regular trims.
quick.risks: Low risk. The main issue is upkeep: Wikipedia notes the style is high-maintenance without naturally straight hair, and humidity can disrupt its shape. Frequent heat straightening can dry hair.

lead: The hime cut, Japanese for princess cut, is a hairstyle with straight, usually cheek-length sidelocks and frontal fringe, with the rest of the hair worn long and straightened.[1]

Its origin is traced to the Japanese Imperial court between 794 and 1185 CE, when noblewomen sometimes grew their hair for life. A coming-of-age ceremony called binsogi cut the hair around the ears shorter, leaving short front locks and longer hair behind. The name hime cut appears to have been applied retroactively, probably because of how princesses were depicted in media.[1][2]
The 1970s idol Megumi Asaoka popularised the look in Japan, and it later spread through Gothic Lolita fashion, cosplay and social media.[1][2]

angle.text: The hime cut changes the outline around the face: the straight fringe and sidelocks create a geometric frame, and the long back adds length. People use it as a styling change to alter how their face and hair read in photos and in person.

infobox: Straight sidelocks, blunt fringe, long straight back

paras: Core elements are a blunt fringe cut straight across the forehead, face-framing sidelocks cut straight at cheek or jaw level, and long, straight hair at the back.[1][2]
Grokipedia contrasts it with curtain bangs, which are softly parted and swept, and with layered styles such as the wolf cut, because the hime cut keeps clean, uniform lines.[2]

Heian-period noblewomen wore very long hair as a status marker, and the binsogi ceremony cut the hair near the ears.[1] In the Edo period the ceremony was held on June 16, often with a relative performing the cut.[1]
The idol Megumi Asaoka made the style her trademark in the 1970s, and a 2022 article described it as trending again.[1]
For people without naturally straight hair, straightening irons, treatments and occasionally extensions are used, and the shape needs frequent touch-ups. Humidity can disrupt it.[1]

The style is common in Lolita fashion, especially Gothic Lolita, where it is seen as more elegant than heavily curled styles. Cosplayers also wear it.[1] Grokipedia says K-pop idols and TikTok have contributed to its recent popularity.[2]
